- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and model overestimates, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent high.
- After a recent spike (sentiment > 0.3), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to counteract bias.
- Model often lags in early days of trend reversal — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% to capture momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent volatility — smooth out sharp swings if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
